name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
      - 'epic/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ******

jobs:
  release-version-integrity:
    name: Release version integrity
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      github.actor == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'release/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out trusted release validation
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |-
            scripts/validate-release-pr.mts
            scripts/release-github-evidence.mts
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Validate version-only release change
        env:
          GITHUB_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_PR_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          RELEASE_PR_MODE: pre-merge
          RELEASE_PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: node scripts/validate-release-pr.mts

  verify:
    name: Verification (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Architecture validates the exact event base/head and accepted epic history.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run policy, type, and test verification
        env:
          HVIR_REPO_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run verify

  electron-smoke:
    name: Electron smoke (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run production Electron workflow
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/production
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke

      - name: Run development renderer Performance Timeline containment
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/development-performance
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:development-performance

      - name: Prove failure and interruption isolation
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:isolation

      - name: Upload bounded Electron failure evidence
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ci-electron-smoke-failure-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  macos-electron-smoke:
    # Temporary reduced gate: terminal-presentation, terminal-lifecycle, and capacity
    # remain available through local commands while their macOS flakes are hardened.
    name: Electron correctness (macOS arm64; temporary reduced gate)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run focused unpackaged Electron scenarios
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/macos-ci
        run: npm run smoke:macos:ci

      - name: Upload bounded macOS Electron failure evidence
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ci-macos-electron-smoke-failure-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  codeql:
    name: CodeQL analysis
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      packages: read
      security-events: write

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4.37.9
        with:
          languages: javascript-typescript

      - name: Analyze
        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4.37.9

  merge-acceptance:
    name: Merge acceptance
    needs:
      - release-version-integrity
      - verify
      - electron-smoke
      - macos-electron-smoke
      - codeql
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out exact head for base ancestry proof
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Require one coherent CI attempt
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node scripts/ci-attempt-evidence.mts

      - name: Require exact candidate ancestry
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          if [[ ! "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ || ! "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Pull request base and head must be full commit SHAs"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            echo "::error::Merge acceptance did not check out the exact pull request head"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA"; then
            echo "::error::The tested pull request base is not an ancestor of its head"
            exit 1
          fi

import console from 'node:console'
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
import process from 'node:process'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { validateAdrLifecycles } from './adr-lifecycle.mts'

const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')
const adrDirectory = join(root, 'docs', 'adr')
const designPath = join(root, 'docs', 'design.md')
const recordName = /^ADR-(\d{3})-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\.md$/
const requiredSections = [
  '## Context',
  '## Decision',
  '## Consequences',
  '## Rejected alternatives',
]
const errors = []

const directoryEntries = readdirSync(adrDirectory).filter((name) =>
  statSync(join(adrDirectory, name)).isFile(),
)
const records = directoryEntries.filter((name) => recordName.test(name)).sort()
const unexpected = directoryEntries
  .filter(
    (name) => !['README.md', 'TEMPLATE.md'].includes(name) && !recordName.test(name),
  )
  .sort()

for (const name of unexpected) {
  errors.push(`docs/adr/${name}: expected ADR-NNN-short-kebab-title.md`)
}

const recordIds = new Map()
const recordSources = new Map()
for (const name of records) {
  const id = recordName.exec(name)[1]
  const path = join(adrDirectory, name)
  const source = readFileSync(path, 'utf8')
  recordSources.set(name, source)
  const previous = recordIds.get(id)
  if (previous) {
    errors.push(`ADR-${id} is duplicated by ${previous} and ${name}`)
  }
  recordIds.set(id, name)

  if (!source.startsWith(`# ADR-${id}: `)) {
    errors.push(`docs/adr/${name}: first heading must be "# ADR-${id}: …"`)
  }

name: Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: current releases package.json; patch/minor/major open a validated release PR.
        required: ******
        type: choice
        options:
          - current

        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Prepare ${{ inputs.bump }} release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
      issues: read
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      ready: ${{ steps.release.outputs.ready }}
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
      sha: ${{ steps.release.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Require the default branch
        env:
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF" != "refs/heads/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
            echo "::error::Run releases from $DEFAULT_BRANCH, not $GITHUB_REF_NAME"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Check out release history
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          fetch-tags: ******

      - name: Select trusted release source
        env:
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ inputs.source_sha }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SOURCE_SHA" ]; then
            exit 0

          if [[ ! "$SOURCE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Release source must be a full commit SHA"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git cat-file -e "$SOURCE_SHA^{commit}"; then
            echo "::error::Release source $SOURCE_SHA is not available"
            exit 1
          fi
          default_sha=$(git rev-parse "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH")

            echo "::error::Release source $SOURCE_SHA is not merged into $DEFAULT_BRANCH"
            exit 1
          fi

        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

        env:

          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ inputs.source_sha }}

          current=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          if [ "$BUMP" = current ]; then
            version=$current
          else
            npm version "$BUMP" --no-git-tag-version --ignore-scripts
            version=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")

          tag="v$version"

          remote_tag_sha=$(git ls-remote origin "refs/tags/$tag^{}" | awk '{print $1}')
          if [ -z "$remote_tag_sha" ]; then
            remote_tag_sha=$(git ls-remote origin "refs/tags/$tag" | awk '{print $1}')
          fi

          if [ "$BUMP" = current ] && [ -n "$remote_tag_sha" ]; then
            if [ -n "$SOURCE_SHA" ] && [ "$remote_tag_sha" != "$SOURCE_SHA" ]; then
              echo "::error::$tag points at $remote_tag_sha, expected release source $SOURCE_SHA"
              exit 1
            fi

            tagged_version=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")

              echo "::error::$tag contains package version $tagged_version, expected $version"
              exit 1

            exit 1

            exit 1

            echo

        if: inputs.bump == 'current'
        timeout-minutes: 5
        env:
          GITHUB_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}

set -uo pipefail

fail=0

report() {
  # $1 = human description, $2 = matching lines (empty = ok)
  if [[ -n "$2" ]]; then
    printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
    printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed 's/^/    /'
    fail=1
  else
    printf '\033[32m✓ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
  fi
}

I'm also noting the ProjectHost abstraction with local and SSH hosts, and the PTY supervisor using node-pty with ghostty for terminals.

Beyond that, I need to capture the broader feature set: harness providers (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, shell, custom commands), git integration with authorization, document review, a viewer supporting markdown/code/diffs, filename search, a web pane proxy, sessions projection, diagnostics, and the `hvir` CLI command. I should verify some specifics for accuracy—how the `hvir` command is installed and invoked, the Node >=24 requirement, platform packaging constraints (macOS arm64, Linux glibc/libstdc++ versions), and the dev setup steps.

I'm also checking the native module build process for `@hvir/rename-noreplace`, which handles atomic renames via renameat2 on Linux and renamex_np on macOS, plus how `npm run dev` checks terminal runtime prerequisites before launching. So architecture:check fails due to missing repo token, check-adrs fails because the ADR directory doesn't exist, and check-seams, typecheck, lint, build, and architecture:report all pass with zero violations. Tests show 2877 passed but 23 failed across 10 files.

Now I'm drafting the README: a concise intro describing hvir as a desktop workbench for git projects that keeps AI coding-agent CLIs and shells alongside files, git history, and diffs across local and SSH-remote folders, built on Electron, currently private at v0.2.3 under MIT license. I'm also outlining the features section covering project registration (local and SSH with config/key/password handling), workspace switching across git worktrees, and PTY-backed terminal panes.

I'm detailing the agent harness support (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, plain shells) with different launch modes, noting these tools aren't bundled and must be installed separately. I'm also describing the file tree and viewer capabilities across Markdown, code, data, and HTML formats, while double-checking exactly how CodeMirror is used in the source view before committing to specific wording.

For the git panel, I'm outlining what it surfaces — status, history, blame, diffs, branches, worktrees — and verifying the scope of allowed mutations (fetch, pull, branch switch, worktree pruning) against the mutation-authorization code to confirm no commit, stage, or push operations exist before stating that claim confidently.

For document review, I want to confirm the delivery modes (copy-only, insert, send-now) against the actual capability constants before describing it. For the web pane, I'll describe it simply as a loopback-only view of locally running dev servers alongside terminals. For sessions, I'm uncertain about the details, so I'll either check the sessions-projection file briefly or keep the description generic to avoid overstating capabilities.

I'm also deciding keyboard-first configuration deserves a mention since keybindings are clearly a settings section, while diagnostics/health reporting seems minor enough to skip for brevity. Then I'm laying out the platform support table: macOS arm64 gets a pkg installer (Intel unsupported), Linux x64 and arm64 get deb packages with glibc/libstdc++ version requirements, and Windows isn't supported at all.

I'm cross-checking the acceptance matrix—Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 for both architectures—against the actual release workflow file to confirm those OS versions are accurate. I'm also reconciling a naming discrepancy between how electron-builder names the macOS package versus how the release assets actually get labeled, so I want to check the release assembly script to pin down the real asset filenames before writing the install instructions.

For usage, I need to look at the native installer template to understand how install.sh expects the package to be provided, plus confirm the uninstall flags (`--uninstall`, `--uninstall --purge`) and the launch command syntax with an optional project directory argument. I'll also note the Node.js 24+ requirement and native build tooling needed for development, without overclaiming whether the macOS build is signed/notarized since that's optional per the build scripts.

For development, I'm checking the prerequisites (C/C++ compiler, Python 3, make, Xcode CLT on macOS) and network requirements during `npm ci` since one dependency comes from a GitHub tarball and Electron needs to be downloaded. I'm mapping out the core commands (`npm ci`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:dir`) and need to verify where `build:dir`'s output actually lands by checking electron-builder.yml rather than assuming it's `dist/`. I also want to confirm the git hooks setup — `npm run hooks:install` wires up a pre-push hook running typecheck and smoke tests, bypassable with `--no-verify`.

Now I'm compiling a table of the most-used npm scripts — dev, build, typecheck, lint, format, test variants, mutation testing, architecture/ADR checks, the full verify gate, smoke test variants, and the platform-specific packaging commands for mac/linux builds.

For testing, I want to note that `npm test` runs ~376 files in Vitest with real child processes, git repos, temp dirs, and loopback sockets, and that smoke tests need `xvfb-run` on Linux or `smoke:macos` on Mac. I should flag that some tests may fail in restricted sandboxes due to loopback binding, temp dir writes, or `ps` usage, and that `verify` needs `docs/adr/` present plus the `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN` env var (which CI supplies).

Now I'm starting the architecture section with a directory/role table, beginning with `src/main` as the Electron main process.

I'm continuing the table with the other source directories — preload bridge, renderer UI, shared contracts, workers, build assets, scripts, and tests — then checking what's actually in `build/` to describe it accurately before moving into the enforced architectural seams around host primitives.

Other seams worth noting: PTYs only spawn through the pty-supervisor, `ssh2` stays confined to the SSH host adapter, only preload touches `ipcRenderer`, and git mutations route through the mutation-authorization module. I want to phrase these carefully without overclaiming what ESLint actually enforces, and I should avoid referencing ADR-010 since that directory isn't present in this checkout. Now I'm moving on to where settings and app state are stored, in Electron's userData directory.

I'm finishing the shortcuts table with more key bindings, noting `Mod` likely maps to Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere (need to verify in keybindings.ts), then moving to security notes about the web pane's loopback-only proxy with authentication, sandboxed HTML previews, and SSH host key verification. I'm also considering a brief troubleshooting section covering platform restrictions and native build errors during `npm ci`.

For releases, I'm thinking through the manual `workflow_dispatch` process with its bump options, which validates the package.json version, builds platform packages, creates a draft release, verifies assets, and publishes afterward — I'll keep this description general but accurate without diving into every workflow detail.

Now I want to verify specifics: asset naming conventions from the release assembly script, the native installer template's usage text, supported OS versions like Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, and the renderer components (CodeMirror, Mermaid, Shiki) claims. I'll batch these checks together — searching the assembly script for platform/hash patterns, reading through the installer template's early lines, and confirming the OS version references in the release workflow.

I'll drop "typography" since it's unverified, and keep the README description generic: appearance, terminal (including a theme gallery), keybindings, git, and harness profiles. I'll also avoid putting test counts in the README since they'd go stale quickly.

Now I'm drafting the README itself — opening with a description of hvir as a desktop workbench for git projects, noting it's built with Electron, React, and TypeScript, private and distributed via GitHub releases at version 0.2.3 under MIT license. Then I'm outlining the Features section covering projects/workspaces, terminal panes with PTY backing and attention states, and the agent harness integrations (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, shell).

I'm continuing the Features list: the viewer (rendered/source/diff views, Markdown with Mermaid, Shiki highlighting, sandboxed HTML previews), document review delivery modes, git browsing with its limited mutation set (fetch, pull, branch switch, worktree prune only), the loopback-only web pane with authenticated proxy, and settings/keybindings.

Now I'm cross-checking platform support claims — macOS requires Apple silicon with Intel refused by the installer, Linux x64/arm64 ship as `.deb` with glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ 12+ requirements, and Windows isn't supported at all.

I'm verifying release acceptance testing runs on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 for both x64 and arm64, and double-checking where the glibc/libstdc++ version requirements come from before listing the actual release artifact filenames for each platform.

The install script verifies the SHA-256 digest of the downloaded package before installing with sudo, and supports flags for updating, uninstalling, or uninstalling with a full purge of settings and cache. Then I'm starting a scripts reference table listing commands like `npm run dev` and `npm run build`.

Then I'll draft a testing section covering how `npm test` exercises real git repos and processes, and how `npm run verify` is CI's full gate, noting that `check-adrs` and `architecture:check` have extra environment requirements.

For smoke tests, I need to explain that they drive the actual Electron app and need a display on Linux (via xvfb-run), with separate macOS and "installed package" variants, plus a caveat about sandboxes blocking loopback binds or temp writes. Then I'm moving into the packaging section, listing the platform-specific pack commands for macOS and Linux builds.

I'm thinking through what packaging actually requires — electron-builder outputs to dist/, and I want to avoid overstating unverified claims about build/ directories and native modules, so I'll leave that detail out. Then I note the release workflow uses assemble:native-release and render:native-installer to produce the asset set including install.sh and SHA256SUMS, without asserting a specific output path I haven't confirmed.

Now I'm sketching the Releases section: a manually triggered workflow where you choose a version bump type, which for patch/minor/major opens a release PR, then builds packages, runs Linux acceptance tests, creates a draft release with assets, verifies it, and publishes. I'm uncertain about whether macOS acceptance runs too, so I'm being careful to only state what I'm confident about regarding the Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 acceptance steps.

For CI, I'm noting that it triggers on PRs to main and epic branches, running verify, Linux smoke tests under Xvfb, a reduced macOS smoke gate, and CodeQL scanning.

Then I'm moving into the architecture overview, describing the three-process structure: the renderer communicating through a preload bridge to the main Electron process, which handles PTYs, git, project hosts, harnesses, sessions, document review, diagnostics, and forked utility workers like git-worker and echo-worker.

Now I'm laying out the directory structure table, covering src/main, src/preload, src/renderer, src/shared, src/workers, build/, packages/rename-noreplace, scripts/, and test/, noting what each contains and that build/ includes Linux and macOS packaging scripts.

Now I'm describing the architectural seam enforcement: `scripts/check-seams.sh` and ESLint rules ensure host primitives like `fs`, `child_process`, `chokidar`, and `node-pty` are only imported by `local-host.ts`, with everything else accessing files and processes through the `ProjectHost` interface implemented by `LocalHost` and `SshHost`.

I want to double-check these claims by grepping for `ssh2`, `node-pty`, `chokidar`, and `child_process` imports to confirm `ssh2` is confined to the SSH adapter, PTYs are only spawned through `pty-supervisor.ts`, `ipcRenderer` is preload-only, and Git mutations route through `mutation-authorization.ts` — since node-pty appears in two overlapping claims that need reconciling before I state them confidently.

Now I'm moving to the configuration and data section: settings live under `userData` (macOS/Linux paths), SSH projects read `~/.ssh/config` and keys, and hvir prompts for passwords, passphrases, keyboard-interactive answers, and host keys, remembering trusted ones and warning on changes. I'm also noting that harness CLIs for cursor/gemini/pi launch with `shellEnvironment: ******`, meaning they inherit the user's login-shell PATH, though I should avoid overgeneralizing this to all providers.

I'm compiling known limitations — no Windows support, no Intel macOS packages, harness CLIs not bundled separately, and limited git write capability — along with a note that `ghostty-web` comes from a forked GitHub release tarball, relevant to prerequisites.

For licensing, I'm confirming it's MIT with details in `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, which cover `ghostty-web` and the `rename-noreplace` binding derived from Skill Steward, though I want to verify the exact license attribution for `ghostty-web` since the grep results were inconclusive on that specific line.

I'm planning the README structure, estimating it'll run around 230 lines, which feels reasonable for a complex app, though I want to trim any redundant sections. Before finalizing, I'm running a verification batch: checking source files for direct imports of node-pty, chokidar, child_process, fs, and ssh2; confirming ipcRenderer usage in the eslint config; checking for libstdc/glibc version references in the installer script and electron-builder config; and inspecting the third-party notices file around the ghostty-web entry to nail down its license line.

# hvir

hvir is a desktop workbench for git projects. It runs AI coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI) and plain shells in terminal panes, next to the files, diffs, and git state they work on. Projects can be local folders or folders on an SSH host.

hvir is built with Electron 43, React 19, and TypeScript. It is version 0.2.3, is not published to npm (`"private": ******`), and ships as native installers. The code is MIT licensed.

## Features

- **Projects and workspaces.** Register local or SSH folders. Each git worktree of a project is a workspace. Switch between workspaces with `Mod+Alt+]` and `Mod+Alt+[`.
- **Terminal panes.** PTY-backed terminals (node-pty) rendered with ghostty-web. Panes report `working`, `bell`, or `idle` attention states. `Mod+Shift+F` searches terminal output.
- **Agent harnesses.** Start Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, a shell, or a custom command in a pane. Launches can be fresh, resumed, or forked. hvir does not bundle the agent CLIs. Install them yourself and make sure they are on `PATH`.
- **Viewer.** Browse files in rendered, source, or diff mode. Markdown supports task lists and Mermaid diagrams, and code is highlighted with Shiki.
- **Document review.** Collect review comments on documents in a workspace and deliver them to a harness as copy-only, insert, or send-now, depending on what the provider supports.
- **Git.** Status, history, commit details, blame, diffs, branches, worktrees, and ignored entries. Git mutations are limited to fetch, pull, branch switch, and worktree prune. The git panel does not commit, stage, or push.
- **Web pane.** View a web server running on this machine. Only loopback addresses (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) are allowed, through an authenticated proxy.
- **Settings.** Appearance, terminal (including a theme gallery), git, keybindings, and harness profiles.

## Platform support

| Platform | Release package | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hvir-<version>-darwin-arm64.pkg` | The installer refuses Intel Macs. |
| Linux, x64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-x64.deb` | Requires glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ 12+. |
| Linux, arm64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-arm64.deb` | Same requirements as x64. |
| Windows | none | Not supported. |

Release acceptance runs on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, on x64 and arm64.

## Installing a release

Each release publishes the package for each platform, plus `install.sh` and `SHA256SUMS`. The installer selects the right package, downloads it over HTTPS, checks its SHA-256 digest, and installs it with `sudo`.

```sh
bash install.sh                      # install or update
bash install.sh --uninstall          # remove hvir; keep settings and cache
bash install.sh --uninstall --purge  # also remove the current user's settings and cache
```

Start hvir from a terminal:

```sh
hvir                    # open hvir
hvir /path/to/project   # open hvir on a local project folder
```

Installed locations:

- **macOS:** the app is at `/Applications/hvir.app`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/local/bin/hvir`.
- **Linux:** the app is under `/opt/hvir`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/bin/hvir`.

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 or newer, and npm.
- macOS or Linux.
- A C/C++ toolchain, `make`, and Python 3 for native modules. On macOS, install the Xcode Command Line Tools.
- GitHub access during `npm ci`. `ghostty-web` is installed from a release tarball on GitHub, and the Electron binary is downloaded during install.

### Setup

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

`postinstall` runs `install:runtime`. That step fetches the Electron binary, then rebuilds `@hvir/rename-noreplace` and `node-pty` against Electron. `predev` and `prebuild` run `scripts/check-terminal-runtime.mts`. If it reports a problem, run `npm ci` again.

### Scripts

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the app in development mode (electron-vite). |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck, then build the main, preload, and renderer bundles into `out/`. |
| `npm run build:dir` | Build, then create an unpacked app with electron-builder in `dist/`. |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for the Node and web configs. |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, including the architecture seam rules. |
| `npm run format` / `format:check` | Prettier, write or check. |
| `npm test` | Vitest suite (`test/`). |
| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. |
| `npm run test:mutation` | Stryker mutation tests, scoped to `src/main/git/git-parsers.ts`. |
| `npm run check-seams` | Architecture seam checks (`scripts/check-seams.sh`). |
| `npm run architecture:report` | Offline architecture hotspot report. |
| `npm run architecture:check` | Enforcing architecture check. Requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. |
| `npm run check-adrs` | Validates ADR file names and headings in `docs/adr/`. |
| `npm run verify` | Full gate: seams, ADRs, architecture check, lint, typecheck, and tests. |
| `npm run smoke` | Build the smoke variant and run the Electron smoke scenarios. |
| `npm run smoke:macos` | macOS subset of the smoke scenarios. |
| `npm run hooks:install` | Install the git pre-push hook. |

The `issue:*` and `project:*` scripts are maintainer tooling for GitHub issues and Projects. They need `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`, and some also need `HVIR_PROJECT_TOKEN`.

### Git hooks

`npm run hooks:install` installs `.githooks/pre-push`. The hook runs `npm run typecheck`, then the Electron smoke suite: `npm run smoke:macos` on macOS, or `npm run smoke` on Linux (under `xvfb-run` when there is no display). Skip it with `git push --no-verify`.

### Code style

Prettier is configured in `.prettierrc.json`: no semicolons, single quotes, trailing commas, two-space indentation, and a 90-column print width.

## Testing

- `npm test` runs the Vitest suite. Many tests use real git repositories, child processes, temporary directories, and loopback sockets.
- `npm run verify` is the full gate that CI runs. Two of its steps depend on more than the source tree: `check-adrs` reads ADRs from `docs/adr/`, and `architecture:check` requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. `npm run architecture:report` runs offline.
- Smoke tests drive the real Electron app through scripted scenarios. On Linux they need a display, so run `xvfb-run -a npm run smoke`. On macOS, run `npm run smoke:macos`. `smoke:linux:installed` and `smoke:macos:installed` check an installed package.
- Tests that bind loopback sockets, write to the OS temp directory, or inspect process groups with `ps` will fail in sandboxes that block those operations.

## Packaging

```sh
npm run pack:mac:arm64         # macOS .pkg for Apple silicon
npm run pack:mac:arm64:signed  # same, with code signing forced
npm run pack:linux:x64         # Linux .deb for x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64       # Linux .deb for arm64
npm run build:dir              # unpacked app, for local checks
```

electron-builder writes to `dist/`. The release workflow uses `render:native-installer` to render `install.sh` from `scripts/native-installer.template.sh`, and `assemble:native-release` to build the full asset set, including `SHA256SUMS`.

## Releases and CI

The **Release** workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is started by hand with a bump choice: `current`, `patch`, `minor`, or `major`. Patch, minor, and major bumps open a validated release PR. The workflow builds the packages, runs install acceptance on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, uploads the full asset set to a draft GitHub release, verifies it, and publishes it.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests to `main` and `epic/**`. It runs `npm run verify` (with `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`), the Linux smoke suite under Xvfb, a reduced macOS smoke gate (`npm run smoke:macos:ci`), and CodeQL.

## Architecture

```
renderer (React) ── window.hvir (preload bridge) ──▶ main process
                                                      ├── windows and IPC authority
                                                      ├── PTYs, git engine, project hosts
                                                      ├── harness providers, sessions, document review
                                                      └── utility processes: git-worker, echo-worker
```

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/main` | Main process: windows, IPC handlers, PTY supervisor, git engine, project hosts, harness providers, document review, sessions, diagnostics. |
| `src/preload` | The `window.hvir` bridge. The only module that uses `ipcRenderer`. |
| `src/renderer` | React UI: terminals, viewer, git panel, settings, dashboards. |
| `src/shared` | Serializable contracts and pure policies shared by more than one process. |
| `src/workers` | Utility-process workers `git-worker.ts` and `echo-worker.ts`, forked by main. |
| `packages/rename-noreplace` | Native addon for no-replace renames, used as the local package `@hvir/rename-noreplace`. |
| `build/` | Packaging resources, including the installed launcher `build/native/hvir-command`. |
| `scripts/` | Build, smoke, acceptance, release, and project-management scripts. |
| `test/` | Vitest suite. |

The seams are enforced by `scripts/check-seams.sh` and by ESLint rules in `eslint.config.mjs`:

- Node file-system, child-process, file-watcher, and `ssh2` imports are confined to `src/main/project-host/`. The rest of the app reaches projects through the `ProjectHost` interface, which `LocalHost` and `SshHost` implement.
- `host.spawnPty` may be called only from `src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts`.
- Only the preload bridge may import `ipcRenderer`.
- Git mutations are authorized in `src/main/git/mutation-authorization.ts`.

## Configuration and security

- Settings and app state live in Electron's `userData` directory: `~/Library/Application Support/hvir` on macOS and `~/.config/hvir` on Linux.
- SSH projects use `~/.ssh/config` and the default keys in `~/.ssh`. hvir prompts for passwords, key passphrases, keyboard-interactive answers, and host-key decisions. Trusted host keys are remembered, and a changed host key raises its own prompt.
- The web pane proxies only loopback addresses, and only for authenticated clients.
- HTML previews run in a sandboxed `hvir-preview` scheme with only `allow-scripts` enabled.

## Keyboard shortcuts

These are the defaults from `src/shared/keybindings.ts`. Change them in Settings → Keybindings. `Mod` means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Find file | `Mod+P` |
| Find in file | `Mod+F` |
| Find in terminal | `Mod+Shift+F` |
| Go to line | `Ctrl+G` |
| Focus terminal | `Mod+J` |
| Toggle terminal focus | `Mod+Shift+J` |
| Focus viewer | `Mod+1` |
| Focus file tree | `Mod+0` |
| Cycle view mode | `Mod+Shift+M` |
| Next / previous workspace | `Mod+Alt+]` / `Mod+Alt+[` |

## Known limitations

- Windows is not supported.
- Packages target Apple-silicon macOS. The installer refuses Intel Macs.
- Agent CLIs are not bundled. Install and configure them yourself.
- The git panel cannot commit, stage, or push. Use your terminal or the agent for those.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Notices for bundled third-party code, including ghostty-web and the rename-noreplace binding derived from Skill Steward, are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

arguments.file_text:
# hvir

hvir is a desktop workbench for git projects. It runs AI coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI) and plain shells in terminal panes, next to the files, diffs, and git state they work on. Projects can be local folders or folders on an SSH host.

hvir is built with Electron 43, React 19, and TypeScript. It is version 0.2.3, is not published to npm (`"private": ******`), and ships as native installers. The code is MIT licensed.

## Features

- **Projects and workspaces.** Register local or SSH folders. Each git worktree of a project is a workspace. Switch between workspaces with `Mod+Alt+]` and `Mod+Alt+[`.
- **Terminal panes.** PTY-backed terminals (node-pty) rendered with ghostty-web. Panes report `working`, `bell`, or `idle` attention states. `Mod+Shift+F` searches terminal output.
- **Agent harnesses.** Start Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, a shell, or a custom command in a pane. Launches can be fresh, resumed, or forked. hvir does not bundle the agent CLIs. Install them yourself and make sure they are on `PATH`.
- **Viewer.** Browse files in rendered, source, or diff mode. Markdown supports task lists and Mermaid diagrams, and code is highlighted with Shiki.
- **Document review.** Collect review comments on documents in a workspace and deliver them to a harness as copy-only, insert, or send-now, depending on what the provider supports.
- **Git.** Status, history, commit details, blame, diffs, branches, worktrees, and ignored entries. Git mutations are limited to fetch, pull, branch switch, and worktree prune. The git panel does not commit, stage, or push.
- **Web pane.** View a web server running on this machine. Only loopback addresses (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) are allowed, through an authenticated proxy.
- **Settings.** Appearance, terminal (including a theme gallery), git, keybindings, and harness profiles.

## Platform support

| Platform | Release package | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hvir-<version>-darwin-arm64.pkg` | The installer refuses Intel Macs. |
| Linux, x64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-x64.deb` | Requires glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ 12+. |
| Linux, arm64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-arm64.deb` | Same requirements as x64. |
| Windows | none | Not supported. |

Release acceptance runs on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, on x64 and arm64.

## Installing a release

Each release publishes the package for each platform, plus `install.sh` and `SHA256SUMS`. The installer selects the right package, downloads it over HTTPS, checks its SHA-256 digest, and installs it with `sudo`.

```sh
bash install.sh                      # install or update
bash install.sh --uninstall          # remove hvir; keep settings and cache
bash install.sh --uninstall --purge  # also remove the current user's settings and cache
```

Start hvir from a terminal:

```sh
hvir                    # open hvir
hvir /path/to/project   # open hvir on a local project folder
```

Installed locations:

- **macOS:** the app is at `/Applications/hvir.app`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/local/bin/hvir`.
- **Linux:** the app is under `/opt/hvir`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/bin/hvir`.

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 or newer, and npm.
- macOS or Linux.
- A C/C++ toolchain, `make`, and Python 3 for native modules. On macOS, install the Xcode Command Line Tools.
- GitHub access during `npm ci`. `ghostty-web` is installed from a release tarball on GitHub, and the Electron binary is downloaded during install.

### Setup

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

`postinstall` runs `install:runtime`. That step fetches the Electron binary, then rebuilds `@hvir/rename-noreplace` and `node-pty` against Electron. `predev` and `prebuild` run `scripts/check-terminal-runtime.mts`. If it reports a problem, run `npm ci` again.

### Scripts

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the app in development mode (electron-vite). |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck, then build the main, preload, and renderer bundles into `out/`. |
| `npm run build:dir` | Build, then create an unpacked app with electron-builder in `dist/`. |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for the Node and web configs. |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, including the architecture seam rules. |
| `npm run format` / `format:check` | Prettier, write or check. |
| `npm test` | Vitest suite (`test/`). |
| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. |
| `npm run test:mutation` | Stryker mutation tests, scoped to `src/main/git/git-parsers.ts`. |
| `npm run check-seams` | Architecture seam checks (`scripts/check-seams.sh`). |
| `npm run architecture:report` | Offline architecture hotspot report. |
| `npm run architecture:check` | Enforcing architecture check. Requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. |
| `npm run check-adrs` | Validates ADR file names and headings in `docs/adr/`. |
| `npm run verify` | Full gate: seams, ADRs, architecture check, lint, typecheck, and tests. |
| `npm run smoke` | Build the smoke variant and run the Electron smoke scenarios. |
| `npm run smoke:macos` | macOS subset of the smoke scenarios. |
| `npm run hooks:install` | Install the git pre-push hook. |

The `issue:*` and `project:*` scripts are maintainer tooling for GitHub issues and Projects. They need `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`, and some also need `HVIR_PROJECT_TOKEN`.

### Git hooks

`npm run hooks:install` installs `.githooks/pre-push`. The hook runs `npm run typecheck`, then the Electron smoke suite: `npm run smoke:macos` on macOS, or `npm run smoke` on Linux (under `xvfb-run` when there is no display). Skip it with `git push --no-verify`.

### Code style

Prettier is configured in `.prettierrc.json`: no semicolons, single quotes, trailing commas, two-space indentation, and a 90-column print width.

## Testing

- `npm test` runs the Vitest suite. Many tests use real git repositories, child processes, temporary directories, and loopback sockets.
- `npm run verify` is the full gate that CI runs. Two of its steps depend on more than the source tree: `check-adrs` reads ADRs from `docs/adr/`, and `architecture:check` requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. `npm run architecture:report` runs offline.
- Smoke tests drive the real Electron app through scripted scenarios. On Linux they need a display, so run `xvfb-run -a npm run smoke`. On macOS, run `npm run smoke:macos`. `smoke:linux:installed` and `smoke:macos:installed` check an installed package.
- Tests that bind loopback sockets, write to the OS temp directory, or inspect process groups with `ps` will fail in sandboxes that block those operations.

## Packaging

```sh
npm run pack:mac:arm64         # macOS .pkg for Apple silicon
npm run pack:mac:arm64:signed  # same, with code signing forced
npm run pack:linux:x64         # Linux .deb for x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64       # Linux .deb for arm64
npm run build:dir              # unpacked app, for local checks
```

electron-builder writes to `dist/`. The release workflow uses `render:native-installer` to render `install.sh` from `scripts/native-installer.template.sh`, and `assemble:native-release` to build the full asset set, including `SHA256SUMS`.

## Releases and CI

The **Release** workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is started by hand with a bump choice: `current`, `patch`, `minor`, or `major`. Patch, minor, and major bumps open a validated release PR. The workflow builds the packages, runs install acceptance on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, uploads the full asset set to a draft GitHub release, verifies it, and publishes it.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests to `main` and `epic/**`. It runs `npm run verify` (with `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`), the Linux smoke suite under Xvfb, a reduced macOS smoke gate (`npm run smoke:macos:ci`), and CodeQL.

## Architecture

```
renderer (React) ── window.hvir (preload bridge) ──▶ main process
                                                      ├── windows and IPC authority
                                                      ├── PTYs, git engine, project hosts
                                                      ├── harness providers, sessions, document review
                                                      └── utility processes: git-worker, echo-worker
```

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/main` | Main process: windows, IPC handlers, PTY supervisor, git engine, project hosts, harness providers, document review, sessions, diagnostics. |
| `src/preload` | The `window.hvir` bridge. The only module that uses `ipcRenderer`. |
| `src/renderer` | React UI: terminals, viewer, git panel, settings, dashboards. |
| `src/shared` | Serializable contracts and pure policies shared by more than one process. |
| `src/workers` | Utility-process workers `git-worker.ts` and `echo-worker.ts`, forked by main. |
| `packages/rename-noreplace` | Native addon for no-replace renames, used as the local package `@hvir/rename-noreplace`. |
| `build/` | Packaging resources, including the installed launcher `build/native/hvir-command`. |
| `scripts/` | Build, smoke, acceptance, release, and project-management scripts. |
| `test/` | Vitest suite. |

The seams are enforced by `scripts/check-seams.sh` and by ESLint rules in `eslint.config.mjs`:

- Node file-system, child-process, file-watcher, and `ssh2` imports are confined to `src/main/project-host/`. The rest of the app reaches projects through the `ProjectHost` interface, which `LocalHost` and `SshHost` implement.
- `host.spawnPty` may be called only from `src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts`.
- Only the preload bridge may import `ipcRenderer`.
- Git mutations are authorized in `src/main/git/mutation-authorization.ts`.

## Configuration and security

- Settings and app state live in Electron's `userData` directory: `~/Library/Application Support/hvir` on macOS and `~/.config/hvir` on Linux.
- SSH projects use `~/.ssh/config` and the default keys in `~/.ssh`. hvir prompts for passwords, key passphrases, keyboard-interactive answers, and host-key decisions. Trusted host keys are remembered, and a changed host key raises its own prompt.
- The web pane proxies only loopback addresses, and only for authenticated clients.
- HTML previews run in a sandboxed `hvir-preview` scheme with only `allow-scripts` enabled.

## Keyboard shortcuts

These are the defaults from `src/shared/keybindings.ts`. Change them in Settings → Keybindings. `Mod` means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Find file | `Mod+P` |
| Find in file | `Mod+F` |
| Find in terminal | `Mod+Shift+F` |
| Go to line | `Ctrl+G` |
| Focus terminal | `Mod+J` |
| Toggle terminal focus | `Mod+Shift+J` |
| Focus viewer | `Mod+1` |
| Focus file tree | `Mod+0` |
| Cycle view mode | `Mod+Shift+M` |
| Next / previous workspace | `Mod+Alt+]` / `Mod+Alt+[` |

## Known limitations

- Windows is not supported.
- Packages target Apple-silicon macOS. The installer refuses Intel Macs.
- Agent CLIs are not bundled. Install and configure them yourself.
- The git panel cannot commit, stage, or push. Use your terminal or the agent for those.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Notices for bundled third-party code, including ghostty-web and the rename-noreplace binding derived from Skill Steward, are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

+hvir is a desktop workbench for git projects. It runs AI coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI) and plain shells in terminal panes, next to the files, diffs, and git state they work on. Projects can be local folders or folders on an SSH host.
+
+hvir is built with Electron 43, React 19, and TypeScript. It is version 0.2.3, is not published to npm (`"private": ******`), and ships as native installers. The code is MIT licensed.
+
+## Features
+
+- **Projects and workspaces.** Register local or SSH folders. Each git worktree of a project is a workspace. Switch between workspaces with `Mod+Alt+]` and `Mod+Alt+[`.
+- **Terminal panes.** PTY-backed terminals (node-pty) rendered with ghostty-web. Panes report `working`, `bell`, or `idle` attention states. `Mod+Shift+F` searches terminal output.
+- **Agent harnesses.** Start Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, a shell, or a custom command in a pane. Launches can be fresh, resumed, or forked. hvir does not bundle the agent CLIs. Install them yourself and make sure they are on `PATH`.
+- **Viewer.** Browse files in rendered, source, or diff mode. Markdown supports task lists and Mermaid diagrams, and code is highlighted with Shiki.
+- **Document review.** Collect review comments on documents in a workspace and deliver them to a harness as copy-only, insert, or send-now, depending on what the provider supports.
+- **Git.** Status, history, commit details, blame, diffs, branches, worktrees, and ignored entries. Git mutations are limited to fetch, pull, branch switch, and worktree prune. The git panel does not commit, stage, or push.
+- **Web pane.** View a web server running on this machine. Only loopback addresses (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) are allowed, through an authenticated proxy.
+- **Settings.** Appearance, terminal (including a theme gallery), git, keybindings, and harness profiles.
+
+## Platform support
+
+| Platform | Release package | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| macOS, Apple silicon | `hvir-<version>-darwin-arm64.pkg` | The installer refuses Intel Macs. |
+| Linux, x64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-x64.deb` | Requires glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ 12+. |
+| Linux, arm64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-arm64.deb` | Same requirements as x64. |
+| Windows | none | Not supported. |
+
+Release acceptance runs on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, on x64 and arm64.
+
+## Installing a release
+
+Each release publishes the package for each platform, plus `install.sh` and `SHA256SUMS`. The installer selects the right package, downloads it over HTTPS, checks its SHA-256 digest, and installs it with `sudo`.
+
+```sh
+bash install.sh                      # install or update
+bash install.sh --uninstall          # remove hvir; keep settings and cache
+bash install.sh --uninstall --purge  # also remove the current user's settings and cache
+```
+
+Start hvir from a terminal:
+
+```sh
+hvir                    # open hvir
+hvir /path/to/project   # open hvir on a local project folder
+```
+
+Installed locations:
+
+- **macOS:** the app is at `/Applications/hvir.app`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/local/bin/hvir`.
+- **Linux:** the app is under `/opt/hvir`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/bin/hvir`.
+
+## Development
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- Node.js 24 or newer, and npm.
+- macOS or Linux.
+- A C/C++ toolchain, `make`, and Python 3 for native modules. On macOS, install the Xcode Command Line Tools.
+- GitHub access during `npm ci`. `ghostty-web` is installed from a release tarball on GitHub, and the Electron binary is downloaded during install.
+
+### Setup
+
+```sh
+npm ci
+npm run dev
+```
+
+`postinstall` runs `install:runtime`. That step fetches the Electron binary, then rebuilds `@hvir/rename-noreplace` and `node-pty` against Electron. `predev` and `prebuild` run `scripts/check-terminal-runtime.mts`. If it reports a problem, run `npm ci` again.
+
+### Scripts
+
+| Command | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| `npm run dev` | Start the app in development mode (electron-vite). |
+| `npm run build` | Typecheck, then build the main, preload, and renderer bundles into `out/`. |
+| `npm run build:dir` | Build, then create an unpacked app with electron-builder in `dist/`. |
+| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for the Node and web configs. |
+| `npm run lint` | ESLint, including the architecture seam rules. |
+| `npm run format` / `format:check` | Prettier, write or check. |
+| `npm test` | Vitest suite (`test/`). |
+| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. |
+| `npm run test:mutation` | Stryker mutation tests, scoped to `src/main/git/git-parsers.ts`. |
+| `npm run check-seams` | Architecture seam checks (`scripts/check-seams.sh`). |
+| `npm run architecture:report` | Offline architecture hotspot report. |
+| `npm run architecture:check` | Enforcing architecture check. Requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. |
+| `npm run check-adrs` | Validates ADR file names and headings in `docs/adr/`. |
+| `npm run verify` | Full gate: seams, ADRs, architecture check, lint, typecheck, and tests. |
+| `npm run smoke` | Build the smoke variant and run the Electron smoke scenarios. |
+| `npm run smoke:macos` | macOS subset of the smoke scenarios. |
+| `npm run hooks:install` | Install the git pre-push hook. |
+
+The `issue:*` and `project:*` scripts are maintainer tooling for GitHub issues and Projects. They need `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`, and some also need `HVIR_PROJECT_TOKEN`.
+
+### Git hooks
+
+`npm run hooks:install` installs `.githooks/pre-push`. The hook runs `npm run typecheck`, then the Electron smoke suite: `npm run smoke:macos` on macOS, or `npm run smoke` on Linux (under `xvfb-run` when there is no display). Skip it with `git push --no-verify`.
+
+### Code style
+
+Prettier is configured in `.prettierrc.json`: no semicolons, single quotes, trailing commas, two-space indentation, and a 90-column print width.
+
+## Testing
+
+- `npm test` runs the Vitest suite. Many tests use real git repositories, child processes, temporary directories, and loopback sockets.
+- `npm run verify` is the full gate that CI runs. Two of its steps depend on more than the source tree: `check-adrs` reads ADRs from `docs/adr/`, and `architecture:check` requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. `npm run architecture:report` runs offline.
+- Smoke tests drive the real Electron app through scripted scenarios. On Linux they need a display, so run `xvfb-run -a npm run smoke`. On macOS, run `npm run smoke:macos`. `smoke:linux:installed` and `smoke:macos:installed` check an installed package.
+- Tests that bind loopback sockets, write to the OS temp directory, or inspect process groups with `ps` will fail in sandboxes that block those operations.
+
+## Packaging
+
+```sh
+npm run pack:mac:arm64         # macOS .pkg for Apple silicon
+npm run pack:mac:arm64:signed  # same, with code signing forced
+npm run pack:linux:x64         # Linux .deb for x64
+npm run pack:linux:arm64       # Linux .deb for arm64
+npm run build:dir              # unpacked app, for local checks
+```
+
+electron-builder writes to `dist/`. The release workflow uses `render:native-installer` to render `install.sh` from `scripts/native-installer.template.sh`, and `assemble:native-release` to build the full asset set, including `SHA256SUMS`.
+
+## Releases and CI
+
+The **Release** workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is started by hand with a bump choice: `current`, `patch`, `minor`, or `major`. Patch, minor, and major bumps open a validated release PR. The workflow builds the packages, runs install acceptance on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, uploads the full asset set to a draft GitHub release, verifies it, and publishes it.
+
+`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests to `main` and `epic/**`. It runs `npm run verify` (with `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`), the Linux smoke suite under Xvfb, a reduced macOS smoke gate (`npm run smoke:macos:ci`), and CodeQL.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+renderer (React) ── window.hvir (preload bridge) ──▶ main process
+                                                      ├── windows and IPC authority
+                                                      ├── PTYs, git engine, project hosts
+                                                      ├── harness providers, sessions, document review
+                                                      └── utility processes: git-worker, echo-worker
+```
+
+| Path | Contents |
+|---|---|
+| `src/main` | Main process: windows, IPC handlers, PTY supervisor, git engine, project hosts, harness providers, document review, sessions, diagnostics. |
+| `src/preload` | The `window.hvir` bridge. The only module that uses `ipcRenderer`. |
+| `src/renderer` | React UI: terminals, viewer, git panel, settings, dashboards. |
+| `src/shared` | Serializable contracts and pure policies shared by more than one process. |
+| `src/workers` | Utility-process workers `git-worker.ts` and `echo-worker.ts`, forked by main. |
+| `packages/rename-noreplace` | Native addon for no-replace renames, used as the local package `@hvir/rename-noreplace`. |
+| `build/` | Packaging resources, including the installed launcher `build/native/hvir-command`. |
+| `scripts/` | Build, smoke, acceptance, release, and project-management scripts. |
+| `test/` | Vitest suite. |
+
+The seams are enforced by `scripts/check-seams.sh` and by ESLint rules in `eslint.config.mjs`:
+
+- Node file-system, child-process, file-watcher, and `ssh2` imports are confined to `src/main/project-host/`. The rest of the app reaches projects through the `ProjectHost` interface, which `LocalHost` and `SshHost` implement.
+- `host.spawnPty` may be called only from `src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts`.
+- Only the preload bridge may import `ipcRenderer`.
+- Git mutations are authorized in `src/main/git/mutation-authorization.ts`.
+
+## Configuration and security
+
+- Settings and app state live in Electron's `userData` directory: `~/Library/Application Support/hvir` on macOS and `~/.config/hvir` on Linux.
+- SSH projects use `~/.ssh/config` and the default keys in `~/.ssh`. hvir prompts for passwords, key passphrases, keyboard-interactive answers, and host-key decisions. Trusted host keys are remembered, and a changed host key raises its own prompt.
+- The web pane proxies only loopback addresses, and only for authenticated clients.
+- HTML previews run in a sandboxed `hvir-preview` scheme with only `allow-scripts` enabled.
+
+## Keyboard shortcuts
+
+These are the defaults from `src/shared/keybindings.ts`. Change them in Settings → Keybindings. `Mod` means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.
+
+| Action | Shortcut |
+|---|---|
+| Find file | `Mod+P` |
+| Find in file | `Mod+F` |
+| Find in terminal | `Mod+Shift+F` |
+| Go to line | `Ctrl+G` |
+| Focus terminal | `Mod+J` |
+| Toggle terminal focus | `Mod+Shift+J` |
+| Focus viewer | `Mod+1` |
+| Focus file tree | `Mod+0` |
+| Cycle view mode | `Mod+Shift+M` |
+| Next / previous workspace | `Mod+Alt+]` / `Mod+Alt+[` |
+
+## Known limitations
+
+- Windows is not supported.
+- Packages target Apple-silicon macOS. The installer refuses Intel Macs.
+- Agent CLIs are not bundled. Install and configure them yourself.
+- The git panel cannot commit, stage, or push. Use your terminal or the agent for those.
+

+MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Notices for bundled third-party code, including ghostty-web and the rename-noreplace binding derived from Skill Steward, are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

result.content:
# hvir

hvir is a desktop workbench for git projects. It runs AI coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI) and plain shells in terminal panes, next to the files, diffs, and git state they work on. Projects can be local folders or folders on an SSH host.

hvir is built with Electron 43, React 19, and TypeScript. It is version 0.2.3, is not published to npm (`"private": ******`), and ships as native installers. The code is MIT licensed.

## Features

- **Projects and workspaces.** Register local or SSH folders. Each git worktree of a project is a workspace. Switch between workspaces with `Mod+Alt+]` and `Mod+Alt+[`.
- **Terminal panes.** PTY-backed terminals (node-pty) rendered with ghostty-web. Panes report `working`, `bell`, or `idle` attention states. `Mod+Shift+F` searches terminal output.
- **Agent harnesses.** Start Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, a shell, or a custom command in a pane. Launches can be fresh, resumed, or forked. hvir does not bundle the agent CLIs. Install them yourself and make sure they are on `PATH`.
- **Viewer.** Browse files in rendered, source, or diff mode. Markdown supports task lists and Mermaid diagrams, and code is highlighted with Shiki.
- **Document review.** Collect review comments on documents in a workspace and deliver them to a harness as copy-only, insert, or send-now, depending on what the provider supports.
- **Git.** Status, history, commit details, blame, diffs, branches, worktrees, and ignored entries. Git mutations are limited to fetch, pull, branch switch, and worktree prune. The git panel does not commit, stage, or push.
- **Web pane.** View a web server running on this machine. Only loopback addresses (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) are allowed, through an authenticated proxy.
- **Settings.** Appearance, terminal (including a theme gallery), git, keybindings, and harness profiles.

## Platform support

| Platform | Release package | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hvir-<version>-darwin-arm64.pkg` | The installer refuses Intel Macs. |
| Linux, x64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-x64.deb` | Requires glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ 12+. |
| Linux, arm64 | `hvir-<version>-linux-arm64.deb` | Same requirements as x64. |
| Windows | none | Not supported. |

Release acceptance runs on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, on x64 and arm64.

## Installing a release

Each release publishes the package for each platform, plus `install.sh` and `SHA256SUMS`. The installer selects the right package, downloads it over HTTPS, checks its SHA-256 digest, and installs it with `sudo`.

```sh
bash install.sh                      # install or update
bash install.sh --uninstall          # remove hvir; keep settings and cache
bash install.sh --uninstall --purge  # also remove the current user's settings and cache
```

Start hvir from a terminal:

```sh
hvir                    # open hvir
hvir /path/to/project   # open hvir on a local project folder
```

Installed locations:

- **macOS:** the app is at `/Applications/hvir.app`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/local/bin/hvir`.
- **Linux:** the app is under `/opt/hvir`, and the `hvir` command is at `/usr/bin/hvir`.

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 or newer, and npm.
- macOS or Linux.
- A C/C++ toolchain, `make`, and Python 3 for native modules. On macOS, install the Xcode Command Line Tools.
- GitHub access during `npm ci`. `ghostty-web` is installed from a release tarball on GitHub, and the Electron binary is downloaded during install.

### Setup

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

`postinstall` runs `install:runtime`. That step fetches the Electron binary, then rebuilds `@hvir/rename-noreplace` and `node-pty` against Electron. `predev` and `prebuild` run `scripts/check-terminal-runtime.mts`. If it reports a problem, run `npm ci` again.

### Scripts

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the app in development mode (electron-vite). |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck, then build the main, preload, and renderer bundles into `out/`. |
| `npm run build:dir` | Build, then create an unpacked app with electron-builder in `dist/`. |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for the Node and web configs. |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, including the architecture seam rules. |
| `npm run format` / `format:check` | Prettier, write or check. |
| `npm test` | Vitest suite (`test/`). |
| `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. |
| `npm run test:mutation` | Stryker mutation tests, scoped to `src/main/git/git-parsers.ts`. |
| `npm run check-seams` | Architecture seam checks (`scripts/check-seams.sh`). |
| `npm run architecture:report` | Offline architecture hotspot report. |
| `npm run architecture:check` | Enforcing architecture check. Requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. |
| `npm run check-adrs` | Validates ADR files in `docs/adr/` (also reads `docs/design.md`). |
| `npm run verify` | Full gate: seams, ADRs, architecture check, lint, typecheck, and tests. |
| `npm run smoke` | Build the smoke variant and run the Electron smoke scenarios. |
| `npm run smoke:macos` | macOS subset of the smoke scenarios. |
| `npm run hooks:install` | Install the git pre-push hook. |

The `issue:*` and `project:*` scripts are maintainer tooling for GitHub issues and Projects. They need `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`, and some also need `HVIR_PROJECT_TOKEN`.

### Git hooks

`npm run hooks:install` installs `.githooks/pre-push`. The hook runs `npm run typecheck`, then the Electron smoke suite: `npm run smoke:macos` on macOS, or `npm run smoke` on Linux (under `xvfb-run` when there is no display). Skip it with `git push --no-verify`.

### Code style

Prettier is configured in `.prettierrc.json`: no semicolons, single quotes, trailing commas, two-space indentation, and a 90-column print width.

## Testing

- `npm test` runs the Vitest suite. Many tests use real git repositories, child processes, temporary directories, and loopback sockets.
- `npm run verify` is the full gate that CI runs. Two of its steps need more than the source tree. `check-adrs` reads `docs/adr/` and `docs/design.md` and fails when they are missing. `architecture:check` requires `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`. The repository does not currently include `docs/`, so `check-adrs` and `verify` fail until those files are restored. `npm run architecture:report` runs offline.
- Smoke tests drive the real Electron app through scripted scenarios. On Linux they need a display, so run `xvfb-run -a npm run smoke`. On macOS, run `npm run smoke:macos`. `smoke:linux:installed` and `smoke:macos:installed` check an installed package.
- Tests that bind loopback sockets, write to the OS temp directory, or inspect process groups with `ps` will fail in sandboxes that block those operations.

## Packaging

```sh
npm run pack:mac:arm64         # macOS .pkg for Apple silicon
npm run pack:mac:arm64:signed  # same, with code signing forced
npm run pack:linux:x64         # Linux .deb for x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64       # Linux .deb for arm64
npm run build:dir              # unpacked app, for local checks
```

electron-builder writes to `dist/`. The release workflow uses `render:native-installer` to render `install.sh` from `scripts/native-installer.template.sh`, and `assemble:native-release` to build the full asset set, including `SHA256SUMS`.

## Releases and CI

The **Release** workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is started by hand with a bump choice: `current`, `patch`, `minor`, or `major`. Patch, minor, and major bumps open a validated release PR. The workflow builds the packages, runs install acceptance on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13, uploads the full asset set to a draft GitHub release, verifies it, and publishes it.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests to `main` and `epic/**`. It runs `npm run verify` (with `HVIR_REPO_TOKEN`), the Linux smoke suite under Xvfb, a reduced macOS smoke gate (`npm run smoke:macos:ci`), and CodeQL.

## Architecture

```
renderer (React) ── window.hvir (preload bridge) ──▶ main process
                                                      ├── windows and IPC authority
                                                      ├── PTYs, git engine, project hosts
                                                      ├── harness providers, sessions, document review
                                                      └── utility processes: git-worker, echo-worker
```

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/main` | Main process: windows, IPC handlers, PTY supervisor, git engine, project hosts, harness providers, document review, sessions, diagnostics. |
| `src/preload` | The `window.hvir` bridge. The only module that uses `ipcRenderer`. |
| `src/renderer` | React UI: terminals, viewer, git panel, settings, dashboards. |
| `src/shared` | Serializable contracts and pure policies shared by more than one process. |
| `src/workers` | Utility-process workers `git-worker.ts` and `echo-worker.ts`, forked by main. |
| `packages/rename-noreplace` | Native addon for no-replace renames, used as the local package `@hvir/rename-noreplace`. |
| `build/` | Packaging resources, including the installed launcher `build/native/hvir-command`. |
| `scripts/` | Build, smoke, acceptance, release, and project-management scripts. |
| `test/` | Vitest suite. |

The seams are enforced by `scripts/check-seams.sh` and by ESLint rules in `eslint.config.mjs`:

- Node file-system, child-process, file-watcher, and `ssh2` imports are confined to `src/main/project-host/`. The rest of the app reaches projects through the `ProjectHost` interface, which `LocalHost` and `SshHost` implement.
- `host.spawnPty` may be called only from `src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts`.
- Only the preload bridge may import `ipcRenderer`.
- Git mutations are authorized in `src/main/git/mutation-authorization.ts`.

## Configuration and security

- Settings and app state live in Electron's `userData` directory: `~/Library/Application Support/hvir` on macOS and `~/.config/hvir` on Linux.
- SSH projects use `~/.ssh/config` and the default keys in `~/.ssh`. hvir prompts for passwords, key passphrases, keyboard-interactive answers, and host-key decisions. Trusted host keys are remembered, and a changed host key raises its own prompt.
- The web pane proxies only loopback addresses, and only for authenticated clients.
- HTML previews run in a sandboxed `hvir-preview` scheme with only `allow-scripts` enabled.

## Keyboard shortcuts

These are the defaults from `src/shared/keybindings.ts`. Change them in Settings → Keybindings. `Mod` means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Find file | `Mod+P` |
| Find in file | `Mod+F` |
| Find in terminal | `Mod+Shift+F` |
| Go to line | `Ctrl+G` |
| Focus terminal | `Mod+J` |
| Toggle terminal focus | `Mod+Shift+J` |
| Focus viewer | `Mod+1` |
| Focus file tree | `Mod+0` |
| Cycle view mode | `Mod+Shift+M` |
| Next / previous workspace | `Mod+Alt+]` / `Mod+Alt+[` |

## Known limitations

- Windows is not supported.
- Packages target Apple-silicon macOS. The installer refuses Intel Macs.
- Agent CLIs are not bundled. Install and configure them yourself.
- The git panel cannot commit, stage, or push. Use your terminal or the agent for those.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Notices for bundled third-party code, including ghostty-web and the rename-noreplace binding derived from Skill Steward, are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

 | `scripts/` | Build, smoke, acceptance, release, and project-management scripts. |
 | `test/` | Vitest suite. |
 
 The seams are enforced by `scripts/check-seams.sh` and by ESLint rules in `eslint.config.mjs`:
 
 - Node file-system, child-process, file-watcher, and `ssh2` imports are confined to `src/main/project-host/`. The rest of the app reaches projects through the `ProjectHost` interface, which `LocalHost` and `SshHost` implement.
 - `host.spawnPty` may be called only from `src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts`.
 - Only the preload bridge may import `ipcRenderer`.
 - Git mutations are authorized in `src/main/git/mutation-authorization.ts`.
 
 ## Configuration and security
 
 - Settings and app state live in Electron's `userData` directory: `~/Library/Application Support/hvir` on macOS and `~/.config/hvir` on Linux.
 - SSH projects use `~/.ssh/config` and the default keys in `~/.ssh`. hvir prompts for passwords, key passphrases, keyboard-interactive answers, and host-key decisions. Trusted host keys are remembered, and a changed host key raises its own prompt.
 - The web pane proxies only loopback addresses, and only for authenticated clients.
 - HTML previews run in a sandboxed `hvir-preview` scheme with only `allow-scripts` enabled.
 
 ## Keyboard shortcuts
 
 These are the defaults from `src/shared/keybindings.ts`. Change them in Settings → Keybindings. `Mod` means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.
 
 | Action | Shortcut |
 |---|---|
 | Find file | `Mod+P` |
 | Find in file | `Mod+F` |
 | Find in terminal | `Mod+Shift+F` |
 | Go to line | `Ctrl+G` |
 | Focus terminal | `Mod+J` |
 | Toggle terminal focus | `Mod+Shift+J` |
 | Focus viewer | `Mod+1` |
 | Focus file tree | `Mod+0` |
 | Cycle view mode | `Mod+Shift+M` |
 | Next / previous workspace | `Mod+Alt+]` / `Mod+Alt+[` |
 
 ## Known limitations
 
 - Windows is not supported.
 - Packages target Apple-silicon macOS. The installer refuses Intel Macs.
 - Agent CLIs are not bundled. Install and configure them yourself.
 - The git panel cannot commit, stage, or push. Use your terminal or the agent for those.
